i.norm: Tests that HTML entity unescaping correctly handles prefix matches per the HTML spec. The HTML spec allows named character references to be matched without a trailing semicolon in text content, but NOT in attribute values. For example, {@code ¬it;} should be parsed as {@code ¬} (U+00AC, NOT SIGN) followed by the literal text {@code it;}, because {@code not} is a valid named entity prefix of {@code notit}. @see jsoup issue #2207 @see HTML spec: character reference state
Input string containing two ambiguous entity references: ¬it; — "notit" is NOT a named entity, but "not" IS (U+00AC, ¬) ∉ — "notin" IS a named entity (U+2209, ∉)
In text (non-strict) mode: ¬it; resolves to ¬ + literal "it;" because "not" is a prefix entity
In attribute (strict) mode: ¬it; stays as-is because attributes require a trailing ";" and "notit" is not a valid entity name; only ∉ (a complete, valid entity) is resolved
In text content (strict=false), the parser applies prefix matching: ¬it; is treated as ¬ (¬) followed by literal "it;"
In attribute values (strict=true), prefix matching is disabled: ¬it; has no valid named entity match with a semicolon, so it is left unchanged
